Subject: Performance SLO qualification & cost levers — Nexa Retail follow-up

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Wanted to capture the key SLOs and next steps so we’re aligned before I loop in Engineering for estimates.

Call recap (short):
- Primary user flows: live product search suggestions (streaming) + checkout fraud-check batch scoring.
- Latency targets: <50ms p95 for suggestion tokens (streaming), <250ms p95 for complete suggestion response; batch scoring SLA is 500ms per batch (50–100 items).
- Throughput/concurrency: expected peak of 600 RPS for suggestions during promotions, baseline 150 RPS; concurrency target ~100 streaming sessions.
- Desired uptime/SLAs: 99.9% during business hours.

Cost levers we discussed to meet SLO: continuous batching for batch scoring, prefix/KV caching for repeated suggestions, model quantization (8-bit q4 variants), and using a lower-latency model variant for streaming where quality tradeoffs are acceptable.

Next steps (agreed):
1) I’ll share a short cost/latency estimate from our infra team (Priyom & Vivek) — includes discrete scenarios for: streaming-optimized model, quantized variant, and cache-enabled picks.
2) Tom will share a 7-day traffic telemetry export (peak hours) and an example suggestions prompt set (Anya to provide).
3) Schedule a technical review with Nexa infra and Redwood infra next week — propose Thu 03/26 10:00 PT.

Attachments: I’m attaching an initial cost worksheet and a traffic heatmap we discussed. These are preliminary and will be refined after the tech review.

If anything above looks off, flag it and I’ll update.

Best,

Hi all —

Thanks for the clear SLOs, Tom. I’ve sketched three scenarios (very high-level) and attached the worksheet with the assumptions. Summary:

Scenario A — Low latency streaming (p95 token <50ms):
- Use streaming-optimized model variant (smaller decoder, prompt engineering for brevity)
- Dedicated pool with higher priority preemption disabled for consistent latency
- Batching disabled on streaming path; aggressive KV/prefix caching for common queries
- Estimated cost: high (15–25% premium vs baseline)

Scenario B — Balanced (p95 token 50–80ms, lower cost):
- Use quantized 8-bit model variant with continuous micro-batching for similar throughput
- Cache hot prefixes + TTL-based caching for suggestions; fall back to streaming variant when cache miss and latency critical
- Estimated cost: medium (baseline)

Scenario C — Cost-optimized (p95 token 80–150ms):
- Use smaller quantized model variants, aggressive batching for token throughput, cache-first responses with async refresh for stale entries
- Utilize model routing to cheaper region/instance types during non-peak
- Estimated cost: low (25–40% savings vs baseline)

Open questions for the tech review we should be prepared to answer:
- Typical token length for suggestion responses and avg tokens per request (affects batching economics).
- Acceptable quality delta between quantized vs FP16 models for suggestions.
- Whether Nexa has local CDN-edge logic to stitch cached responses (helps reduce p95 further).

I’ve attached the spreadsheet with per-scenario latency/cost assumptions and a simple amortized cost-per-10k-requests calculation. Vivek, please add any infra-level concerns (autoscale, prewarm) in the doc before the call.

Cheers,
Priyom

Quick infra notes before the tech review:

- Autoscale/backfill: We recommend a dedicated pool with burstable capacity and an aggressive prewarm window for promo events. Will need Nexa’s 7-day telemetry to size prewarms correctly.
- KV cache: prefix caching will give the best p95 improvement for suggestions — we should prioritize common query detection and TTLs.
- Continuous batching: viable for batch scoring (easy wins) and for balanced streaming scenario with micro-batches (10–20ms added latency typical).
- Quantization: 8-bit q4 variants usually maintain perceptual quality for short suggestion completions; we should run a small eval set.
- Fallback routing: configure streaming -> quantized -> smaller model fallback chain for graceful degradation.

I’ve annotated the attached sheet with an infra checklist. Also added a column showing expected latency bump from micro-batching at different batch sizes.

See you on Thu — I’ll join the invite once Marissa sends it.

Vivek Kulkarni
